children: Al Suwadi Power Company has confirmed receiving in-principle regulatory approval for the proposed merger with Al Batinah Power Company.
The approval was granted by the Financial Services Authority (FSA), Oman’s capital markets regulator, the company said in a statement to the Muscat Stock Exchange.
Al Suwadi Power is currently awaiting the required approvals from other relevant authorities for the proposed merger.
The planned merger is also subject to compliance with the Companies Law and any other relevant legislation, the statement added.
In May, the two companies commenced the preliminary assessment of a potential merger.

The companies have considered the synergies and operational efficiencies arising from the proposed merger as part of the economics of their new 15-year power purchase agreements (PPAs) with the state-run Nama Power and Water Procurement Company.
Al Suwadi Power and Al Batinah Power operate the 750 megawatt (MW) Barka III Independent Power Plant (IPP) and the 750MW Sohar II IPP, respectively.
In April 2026, the two companies signed new 15-year PPAs with Nama PWP. The contracts are set to commence on 1 April, 2028, and will remain in effect until 31 March 2043.

title: Oman's Al Suwadi Power gets FSA nod on merger with Al Batinah Power
